claims.text: Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled annealing can refine the grain structure of HfNbTaTiZr.
Grain refinement increases grain-boundary density in HfNbTaTiZr.
Increasing grain-boundary density enhances grain-boundary pinning.
Grain-boundary pinning restricts dislocation mobility in HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Restricted dislocation mobility caused by grain boundaries reduces the effective thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr.
Restricted dislocation mobility caused by grain boundaries increases the elevated-temperature yield strength of HfNbTaTiZr.
Increased grain-boundary density enhances the strain-rate sensitivity of HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures.
Grain-boundary pinning delays the onset of plasticity under high-temperature conditions.
Fine-grained HfNbTaTiZr will have a lower thermal expansion coefficient than a coarse-grained baseline.
Fine-grained HfNbTaTiZr will have a higher elevated-temperature yield strength than a coarse-grained baseline.
The predicted grain-size effects should hold between approximately 700 K and 1100 K at strain rates typical of high-temperature mechanical testing.
Outside the proposed temperature and strain-rate range, additional deformation mechanisms may dominate.
Twin boundaries or recovery processes may independently influence the mechanical and thermal responses.
Grain size and grain-boundary density can be quantified using TEM and EBSD.
